summary:
Held 0 of today's 10 biggest UK/EU movers.

• 6 upside misses — BNZL.L +5%, RWE.DE +4%, SSE.L +4%, HWDN.L +3%, TSCO.L +3%. These cleared the universe screen but no strategy picked them up; the morning brief either filtered them on a catalyst/RSI/earnings rule or had nothing positive to trigger an entry.

• 4 downside moves (AKZA.AS -17%, PRX.AS -6%, G24.DE -5%, ADYEN.AS -5%) are unreachable on a long-only basket — no mechanism to express a short or pair-trade.

• Most instructive miss: AKZA.AS (-17.22%) — Nippon Paint and Sherwin-Williams formally withdrew their joint €73/share all-cash takeover bid on 3 June after AkzoNobel's board rejected both offers; shares continued unwinding the acquisition premium through 5 June close. Why we passed: Outside any active strategy's universe. AKZA.AS is a large-cap STOXX 600 Dutch industrials name trading at an M&A-inflated price; the -17% move is a pure contested-takeover-premium collapse, structurally unreadable from price action, volume, or momentum signals in advance.

top_movers.catalyst: Macro defensive rotation into FTSE 100 distributors; no company RNS on Jun 5. Extended Jun 3 +3% move; last catalyst Apr 22 Q1 statement reaffirming FY26 guidance (+2% underlying revenue growth).
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe. BNZL.L is a £7.6B FTSE 100 support-services large-cap; Jun 5 move followed a Jun 3 +3% session, so RSI ceiling and gap-extension filters would likely have flagged it as over-extended at open.
top_movers.suggestion: Expand the large-cap UK strategy's universe to include FTSE 100 Support Services names (e.g. BNZL.L); then apply a defensive-rotation entry filter: day-2 continuation allowed if prior session gain ≥ 2% and RSI < 72.

top_movers.catalyst: Jefferies raised RWE price target €61→€63 (Buy maintained) on Jun 5, calling the ~10% April-peak pullback a buying opportunity; triggered two days after the €1.5B share buyback programme completed.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — RWE is a DAX large-cap integrated utility (~€30B mkt cap). Analyst-upgrade moves require pre-event positioning or sub-minute reactive signals unavailable for names outside the scanning universe.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a DAX/STOXX utility watchlist tier that fires on analyst price-target upgrades ≥5% coinciding with ≥8% prior-30-day drawdown; size at ¼ normal notional to contain sector-concentration risk.

top_movers.catalyst: SSE FY2026 EPS of 153.5p beat 147–152p guidance; Board lifted dividend 7%; JPMorgan raised PT to 2600p and RBC to 2475p post-results, sustaining buying into early June.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — SSE.L is a FTSE 100 regulated utility (~£22B cap) too low-volatility for momentum/mean-reversion screens. The gain also lagged the May 28 earnings release by 5 sessions as analyst upgrades trickled in, defeating post-close signal entry.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a post-results analyst-sweep rule: admit large-cap names with EPS beat ≥3% and ≥2 sell-side PT upgrades within 5 sessions of results; enter next open only if RSI < 65 and price < 1.05× results-day close.

top_movers.catalyst: Howden Joinery announced acquisition of online kitchen retailer DIY Kitchens for £390m (£292.5m cash + £97.5m shares), expected immediately EPS-accretive; concurrent £50m share buyback commenced 3 Jun 2026.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — HWDN.L is a FTSE 100 large-cap (~£4-5bn) UK kitchen-fittings retailer not covered by current strategy universes. Move was M&A-driven via an RNS filing; pre-market positioning is structurally impossible for post-signal strategies.
top_movers.suggestion: Integrate an LSE RNS feed monitor: when a universe-adjacent name (FTSE 100/250, UK consumer/building materials sector) files a material acquisition or buyback RNS, auto-add to news-reactive strategy's watchlist and allow same-session entry within 30 minutes of filing.

top_movers.catalyst: Ongoing £750m share buyback (~2M shares repurchased daily at escalating prices: 433p on 2 Jun → 446p on 4 Jun) provided consistent mechanical buy pressure, ratcheting the price up through the week.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe. TSCO.L is a FTSE 100 large-cap defensive grocer; the move was buyback-driven and gradual rather than a sharp gap or momentum breakout, offering no high-conviction signal for short-horizon momentum or news-reactive strategies.
top_movers.suggestion: Add an RNS buyback-flow filter: names executing ≥0.03% of float/day via 'Transaction in Own Shares' disclosures qualify for a low-volatility trend overlay, capturing steady buyback-supported climbs without requiring a gap signal.

top_movers.catalyst: Weekly 'Transaction in Own Shares' RNS (07:00 BST) confirmed 6.08M shares repurchased at 297–302p in the prior week, providing visible price support one day after the 9.6p final dividend ex-date (4 June) reset the stock lower.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — SBRY is a FTSE 100 large-cap UK grocery staple (~£6bn mkt cap) with muted day-to-day volatility; the +2.80% move was mechanical (buyback floor meeting post-ex-div reset), not a clean momentum breakout or pre-announced catalyst that a news-reactive or gap-and-go filter would surf
top_movers.suggestion: Add a 'buyback-support' scan: when a LSE name's weekly Transaction in Own Shares RNS discloses ≥5M shares bought at a VWAP within 2% of the prior session close, flag it for the momentum strategy's universe that day with a half-size position cap.

top_movers.catalyst: Nippon Paint and Sherwin-Williams formally withdrew their joint €73/share all-cash takeover bid on 3 June after AkzoNobel's board rejected both offers; shares continued unwinding the acquisition premium through 5 June close.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe. AKZA.AS is a large-cap STOXX 600 Dutch industrials name trading at an M&A-inflated price; the -17% move is a pure contested-takeover-premium collapse, structurally unreadable from price action, volume, or momentum signals in advance.
top_movers.suggestion: Maintain a live contested-takeover watchlist; when ≥2 competing bids exist, flag the name as news-reactive-only and trigger a short entry within 5 min of a bid-withdrawal headline if the pre-open indicated gap exceeds -10%, capped at a 2-session holding window.

top_movers.catalyst: Tencent (0700.HK) extended its Q1 selloff to multi-month lows (430 HKD, Jun 2) on a revenue miss (¥196.5B vs ¥199B est.) and AI competition from ByteDance; dragged PRX as Tencent represents ~85% of Prosus NAV.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe. Prosus is a Dutch holding company whose value tracks Tencent HK (~85% NAV). EU strategies typically filter NAV proxies for non-European underlyings; the alpha is captured at HK open, not EU close.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a `china_tech_proxy` screen: if 0700.HK closes ≥2% lower overnight, flag PRX.AS for pre-open universe inclusion — wiring the HK signal into the EU universe gate would have caught today's 5.5% gap.

top_movers.catalyst: AGM pre-meeting buyback blackout began June 5–17, suspending Scout24's active €250M second-tranche share repurchase programme and removing its mechanical daily demand floor; no new fundamental news on the day.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — G24.DE is a mid-cap MDAX classifieds/proptech name (~€5B mktcap) likely below the bot's sector-coverage or liquidity threshold. The drop was a mechanical supply/demand event (buyback pause), not a momentum or news signal the bot's filters monitor.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a 'buyback blackout' pre-signal: flag MDAX/SDAX names with an active ≥€100M repurchase tranche whose AGM suspension window starts within 2 sessions, and route them to the short watchlist for that day — buyback-pause selloffs are dateable and repeatable.

top_movers.catalyst: Continued bleed from May 27 CFO Tandowsky surprise departure (stock fell 3% on day-of); compounded by Q1 2026 net revenue miss (€620.8M vs €621.3M est) and ongoing sell-side price-target cuts averaging -19% over 3 months.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — ADYEN.AS is a ~€28B large-cap Euronext Amsterdam payments processor likely above the bot's market-cap band or outside its sector filters. The June 5 leg is a multi-day continuation drift, not a sharp same-session catalyst gap that news-reactive entry signals target.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a 'leadership-exit trailing window' rule: flag names with a CFO/CEO surprise departure in the prior 5–10 sessions and unresolved downward price drift >3%; a short-side mean-reversion entry on day 5–7 post-announcement captures the delayed institutional unwind.
